name: L-Asparaginase

overview.mechanism: Depletes circulating asparagine, affecting leukemic cells unable to synthesize sufficient asparagine.
uses: Asparaginase is used within multi-agent ALL chemotherapy; preparation and protocol must be identified.

sources.citation: FDA Philippines product records preserved in website registry shards; exact generic heading inspected 2026-11-25. Cached identity information, not a new verification of present registration validity or product insert.
FDA. ELSPAR(asparaginase) US prescribing information, revisedJuly 2013. Historical E.coli-derived product comparator; verified 2026-11-25.
van der Sluis IM, et al. Consensus expert recommendations for identification and management of asparaginase hypersensitivity and silent inactivation. Haematologica.2016;101:279–285. PMID 26928249.

draft_notes: Exact Philippine product insert governs dosing. No preparation, species, route or dialysis regimen transferred from a different product.

revision_log.change: New source-linked descriptive monograph, exact cached product identity separated from comparator US labeling or clinical research.
revision_log.approved_by: W. G. M. Rivero, MD (delegated source-verification workflow; executed by Codex, 2026-11-25)

usual_adult_dose.dose: No universal regimen assigned. Confirm species/preparation and protocol; native E.coli, Erwinia and PEG preparations are not interchangeable [[ELSPAR]]

contraindications: Historical ELSPAR comparator: serious allergy to ELSPAR/E.coli-derived asparaginase; prior asparaginase-associated serious thrombosis, pancreatitis or serious hemorrhage [[ELSPAR]]

common: Historical ELSPAR label lists allergy, hyperglycemia, pancreatitis, CNS thrombosis, coagulopathy and abnormal liver tests among common reactions; no frequency transfer to unidentified Philippine preparations [[ELSPAR]]
serious: Anaphylaxis, fulminant pancreatitis, hepatic failure, ketoacidosis and PRES [[ELSPAR]]

monitoring: ELSPAR reference: observe one hour after administration; monitor glucose, coagulation, hepatic enzymes/bilirubin; evaluate abdominal pain and neurologic symptoms [[ELSPAR]]

key_interactions.effect: Inappropriate interchange risks underexposure or overdose [[ELSPAR]]
key_interactions.action: Confirm formulation and route before administration [[ELSPAR]]

evidence.title: Identity and safety evidence
evidence.intro: No CKD, HD, PD or CRRT regimen is inferred.

rows.intervention: L-Aspase, Onconase 10, Apospagin 5000/10000, Oncoase, Carcinase, L-Aspiget, Oncoginase and Celginase/unbranded records; generally 5000 or 10000 IU powder, often IM/IV.
rows.findings: The cached generic/strength fields do not establish organism source, PEG status or bioequivalence.
rows.limitations: Historical ELSPAR is a safety comparator only; no ELSPAR or PEG dose schedule imported.

rows.design: PubMed-verified guidance addressing E.coli- and Erwinia-derived preparations.
rows.intervention: Assessment of clinical hypersensitivity and silent inactivation.
rows.findings: Neutralizing antibodies may reduce enzyme activity without an evident allergic reaction. Absence of symptoms alone therefore does not document sustained asparaginase activity.
rows.limitations: Product- and protocol-specific activity monitoring decisions remain necessary; no assay target or timing invented here.
